column1: # ZAP baseline rules for .github/workflows/dast-scan.yml (passed as `-c`).
# Format: one rule per line, TAB-separated —
#   <ZAP plugin id>
# Lines starting with `#` are comments. Plugin ids: https://www.zaproxy.org/docs/alerts/
# The scan fails on any alert not listed here (fail_action: true), so this
# file is the DAST counterpart of .github/trivy-allowlist: every entry names
# the alert it accepts and why the finding is not exploitable in Turbo EA's
# deployment shape, and every entry is re-read at the quarterly allowlist
# review. Prefer fixing over listing — a missing header is a one-line nginx
# change. Never IGNORE a High-risk alert; downgrade it to WARN at most, with
# the mitigation written next to it.
# Seeded from the first dispatch run (2026-09-30, run 36746175997): 0 FAIL,
# 7 WARN. Two of the seven were fixed at the source instead of listed here —
# 10036 (Server header leaked the nginx version: `server_tokens off`) and
# 10055 (the app and /api CSPs carried no `frame-ancestors`; they do now).
# The five below are informational or not applicable to this deployment
# shape; each is Low or Informational risk in ZAP's own rating.
# Non-Storable Content. Informational. The API answers with
# Cache-Control: no-store on purpose — session-bound JSON must never land in a
# shared cache — and ZAP reports exactly that. Reviewed 2026-09-30.

column3: API responses are deliberately no-store; informational

column1: # Timestamp Disclosure - Unix. Low. The one hit is a 10-digit integer constant
# inside the minified SPA bundle (a library's epoch constant), not a leaked
# server time. Reviewed 2026-09-30; re-check if the hit moves to an API route.

column3: integer constant in the minified bundle, not a server timestamp

column1: # Modern Web Application. Informational. States that the site is a
# JavaScript application and the classic spider will see little; it is, and
# that is why the AJAX spider runs. Reviewed 2026-09-30.

column3: informational: it is an SPA, the AJAX spider is on

column1: # Sub Resource Integrity Attribute Missing. Medium in ZAP's rating, not
# actionable here: the only cross-origin <link> tags are the Google Fonts
# stylesheets (Material Symbols, Inter), whose CSS is generated per user
# agent, so no integrity hash can be pinned. font-src / style-src in the CSP
# restrict those origins to fonts.googleapis.com and fonts.gstatic.com.
# Reviewed 2026-09-30; drops out if the fonts are ever self-hosted.

column3: Google Fonts stylesheets cannot carry an SRI hash; origins are CSP-pinned

column1: # Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy Header Missing. Low. COEP require-corp would
# refuse every cross-origin subresource that lacks CORP headers (the fonts
# above, the DrawIO assets) and pairs with COOP, which `location /` must
# never carry: the SSO popup relays its result to window.opener (#1126).
# Reviewed 2026-09-30.

column3: COEP would break fonts and the SSO popup relay; COOP is off by design
